objective: Verify local Cloud IaC module archive bytes against release-index archive_sha256 before serving /artifacts/modules/<archive>.zip responses, preserving local-filesystem-only scope and no production/object-store/signing claims.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu module registry download responses provide a location from which module source is downloaded; relative locations are allowed.
OpenTofu can install modules from archive packages such as .zip sources.
Artifact integrity/provenance expectations only reduce risk when artifacts are actually verified against expected digests/provenance.

implemented_claims: The app stores release-index archive_sha256 with each prevalidated local archive artifact.
The /artifacts/modules/{archive_file} route computes SHA-256 over local file bytes at request time before serving.
Digest mismatch returns 409 {"error":"artifact_digest_mismatch"} and does not serve the mismatched bytes.
Matching local archive bytes continue to return 200 with content-type archive/zip.
Manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit-chain scope record local request-time digest verification only.
explicit_non_claims: no database adapter or persistent registry store
no production authentication runtime or Cedar runtime integration
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation verification
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution
no measured SLO, DR, sharding execution, tenant migration, or capacity telemetry
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence
no aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all success claim for current worktree
false_green_findings_closed: Previously the app could serve a locally drifted archive file after gate-time archive verification; the request path now recomputes SHA-256 and fails closed on mismatch.

The previous module_registry_app_scope still described source_path-to-git source mapping even after artifact-download alignment; the manifest scope now records archive_file-derived /artifacts/modules locations and digest verification.
Positive artifact tests now use the actual SHA-256 digest of the served fixture bytes instead of an arbitrary hex placeholder.
known_gaps: Digest verification is local request-time SHA-256 checking only; it is not module signing, SLSA provenance, VSA, or cosign verification.
The local artifact route still reads archive bytes into memory and is not an object-store, CDN, or production streaming implementation.
Production authentication, persistence, signed releases, OpenTofu plan/apply, provider runtime, live GitOps/Kubernetes rollout evidence, and FD-001 tenant workload hosting remain future work.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required and aggregate gate run-all are not claimed by this slice.

findings: Kept the slice direct: preserve existing artifact route shape and add a single digest check before serving bytes.
Moves the module-registry seam closer to supply-chain safe artifact delivery by checking expected local archive digests at request time.
RED proved tampered local bytes were served; GREEN proves digest drift fails closed with no archive bytes served.
Existing download URL shape and successful local fixture behavior remain unchanged for matching bytes.
Focused app tests now cover positive artifact serving, invalid/unknown/missing artifacts, and digest mismatch. Broader gates are recorded in verification as they run.

alternatives_named: Keep relying only on gate-time archive verification
Add local request-time SHA-256 verification before serving bytes
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Local request-time digest verification closes the immediate served-byte drift false green without overclaiming production signing or object storage.
rejected_reasons: Gate-only verification cannot detect local drift between gate execution and app request.
Object-store/signing would require larger runtime, credential, and attestation surfaces outside this local-foundation slice.

findings: The route still validates requested archive names and configured archive paths, then adds digest verification before returning bytes.
Digest check reads/hashes local foundation archive bytes in memory; no throughput/SLO claim is made. Object-store streaming remains future work.
Digest verification is evidence toward supply-chain hygiene but not a compliance certification, signature verification, SLSA level, or VSA claim.
OpenTofu module-registry download JSON and relative artifact path behavior remain unchanged for valid artifacts.
Digest drift returns a stable JSON error code artifact_digest_mismatch for local operator diagnosis without leaking expected/actual digest values.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, app source/tests, manifest/catalog/tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain rows.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root hub and operating contract; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
Adds sha2 only at the app/composition-root layer for local artifact digest verification; no tokio/hyper/provider dependency leakage is introduced.

review_findings: No critical/high issues found in self-review. Digest verification is intentionally local, in-memory, and non-SLO; object-store streaming and signing remain explicit future work.
